claim: menu_driver() accepts an ascii character (HOWTO); it accumulates printable ASCII characters (Writing Programs)
quote: HOWTO: "the value can be either a menu navigational request, an ascii character, or a KEY_MOUSE..."; ncurses-intro: "menu_driver() logic tries to accumulate printable ASCII characters passed in in that buffer"; menu_driver(3X): "If the second argument is a printable character, the code appends it to the pattern buffer"; m_driver.c uses isprint on the character.
earlier: After only the HOWTO line I would have treated 'ascii character' as vague; the intro, man page, and m_driver.c confirm both phrasings describe the same printable pattern-buffer path.

claim: Example 21. Milt Columnar Menus Example
quote: Section heading is "17.6. Multi Columnar Menus" but the example title is "Example 21. Milt Columnar Menus Example".
earlier: Without comparing the section title I might have accepted 'Milt' as a proper name; the adjacent "Multi Columnar" heading shows it is a misspelling.

claim: The Menu Basics listing frees only items 0 and 1 of five, and calls free_menu() on a menu that is still posted
quote: Example 18 builds five choices, post_menu(my_menu), then free_item(my_items[0]); free_item(my_items[1]); free_menu(my_menu); with no unpost_menu. free_menu(3X) returns E_POSTED if the menu is posted; free_item(3X) returns E_CONNECTED while an item is still connected.
earlier: Counting only the free_item calls would miss that free_menu runs while still posted; menu_new(3X) E_POSTED confirms that part of the claim.

claim: The Multi Valued Menus listing frees only items 0 and 1 of eight, and calls free_menu() on a menu that is still posted
quote: Example 22 has eight choices, post_menu(my_menu), then free_item(my_items[0]); free_item(my_items[1]); free_menu(my_menu); and no unpost_menu.
earlier: Same pattern as Menu Basics; opening the Multi Valued listing alone already bears the claim out.

claim: The Menu Options listing frees the items before the menu
quote: unpost_menu(my_menu); then for-loop free_item(my_items[i]); then free_menu(my_menu). free_menu disconnects the item array; free_item returns E_CONNECTED while items remain connected.
earlier: Seeing unpost_menu first I might have thought cleanup was fine; free_item-before-free_menu is still the wrong order per the man pages.

claim: The Menu User Pointer listing frees the items before the menu
quote: unpost_menu(my_menu); for-loop free_item(...); free_menu(my_menu); same connected-item hazard as L50.
earlier: Same conclusion from the listing alone; man pages only confirm why the order is wrong.

claim: The Menu User Pointer listing stores the address of `MY_DATA data`, a variable local to the loop body, as each item's user pointer and calls through it after the loop
quote: Inside for (i = 0; i < n_choices; ++i) { MY_DATA data = {func}; ... set_item_userptr(my_items[i], (void *) &data); } later data = item_userptr(cur); data->my_func(...). mitem_new(3X) warns against names/descriptions on a routine's stack; the same lifetime bug applies to the user pointer.
earlier: The set_item_userptr line alone shows a pointer to loop-scoped storage; the Enter handler confirms the later call-through.

claim: The list of menu options ends at O_NONCYCLIC
quote: HOWTO lists O_ONEVALUE through O_NONCYCLIC and stops. menu_opts(3X) continues with O_MOUSE_MENU after O_NONCYCLIC.
earlier: HOWTO alone shows the list ending at O_NONCYCLIC; the man page shows that ending omits a real option.

claim: The mouse requests are quoted from an older menu_driver(3X), with its line breaks and soft hyphens (decora­tion), and without the double-click on an item
quote: HOWTO quote ends at positioning the cursor on a clicked item and contains the soft-hyphenated "decora­tion". Current menu_driver(3X) additionally documents double-click on an item generating REQ_TOGGLE_ITEM and returning E_UNKNOWN_COMMAND.
earlier: The missing double-click sentence is visible from the HOWTO quote alone; the soft hyphen and current man page seal the 'older copy' reading.

claim: A link to text mode dos games at http://www.jersey.net/~debinjoe/games/
quote: "similar to those text mode dos games" links to http://www.jersey.net/~debinjoe/games/.
earlier: Nothing earlier; the HOWTO line is the whole claim. Link liveness was not required to confirm the printed URL.

claim: the drive assumes it is an application-specific command
quote: At this commit: "the driver assumes it is an application-specific command". Parent of 3b3c5fd89 ("man: fix two typos in menu_driver(3X)") had "the drive assumes".
earlier: Reading only HEAD I would have said disagrees; the pre-fix revision shows the claim matched an earlier man page.

claim: menu_driver return one of the following error codes
quote: At this commit: "menu_driver returns one of the following error codes". Pre-fix text was "menu_driver return one of the following error codes".
earlier: HEAD alone contradicts the claim; the typo-fix parent bears it out historically.

claim: replace a panel's window with a different window by calling `replace_window`
quote: Intro: "You can replace a panel's window with a different window by calling replace_window." The library exports replace_panel, not replace_window.
earlier: The intro wording alone looks authoritative; panel.h/man show the real name is replace_panel.

claim: The `stsdcr` window is a special case
quote: "The stsdcr window is a special case. It is considered below all panels." The next sentence correctly says stdscr.
earlier: If I stopped at the first sentence I might invent a stsdcr object; the following stdscr reference shows it is a typo.

claim: The `panel_update` code ignores hidden panels
quote: Intro names "panel_update". The API is update_panels(); p_update.c walks the linked stack only, and hide_panel unlinks panels, so hidden panels are skipped—but not under the name panel_update.
earlier: Trusting the intro name I would have matched; the man page and p_update.c show the function is update_panels.

claim: You cannot do `top_panel()` or `bottom_panel` on a hidden panel()
quote: Intro forbids both calls on a hidden panel. panel(3X) PORTABILITY: show_panel and top_panel "work equally well with displayed or hidden panels". top_panel calls show_panel; bottom_panel re-links an unlinked panel at the bottom.
earlier: The intro sentence alone would match the claim as printed; the implementation and PORTABILITY note contradict it for ncurses.

claim: Note that `wgetch` automatically calls `wrefresh`
quote: Intro: "Note that wgetch automatically calls wrefresh." curs_getch(3X): if the window "has been moved or modified since the last call to wrefresh, curses calls wrefresh on it."
earlier: Without the man page I would treat 'automatically' as unconditional; the man page narrows it to dirty/moved windows, which still supports the intro's panels warning.

claim: For some reason the function `panel_hidden()` which tells whether a panel is hidden or not is not working, with a link to a 1999 bug report
quote: HOWTO: "panel_hidden() ... is not working" plus a 1999 geocrawler link. panel_hidden() returns FALSE if linked and TRUE if not; the implementation is straightforward IS_LINKED logic.
earlier: Believing the HOWTO I would have matched; p_hidden.c and panel(3X) show the function works in this tree.

claim: /* Update the stacking order. 2nd panel will be on top */ (also in the moving and hiding listings)
quote: All three listings push panels 0, then 1, then 2 ("Order is bottom up") so the third panel is on top, yet each comment says "2nd panel will be on top".
earlier: Seeing the comment in one listing I might only note its presence; comparing push order shows the comment is false, not merely repeated.

claim: The program reads a panel's position and size from its PANEL_DATA when it comes to the top, but never writes them back, so a moved panel jumps back to where it started the next time it is moved
quote: set_user_ptrs writes x,y,w,h once. Tab handler reloads newx/newy/neww/newh from top->x etc. move_panel updates use locals only; no assignment back into PANEL_DATA. Resize replaces the window but still does not update ptr fields.
earlier: Noticing reads on tab without checking writes would leave the jump undemonstrated; searching for assignments to top->x/ptrs[i].x after init finds none.

claim: "Show or Hide a window with 'a'(first window)  'b'(Second Window)  'c'(Third Window)", 83 characters on an 80-column screen
quote: mvprintw string is exactly that text; character length is 83.
earlier: Reading the line without counting might leave the 80-column claim open; strlen confirms 83.

claim: Mainpulate; is used to created panels; removes it form the stack; Entered Resizing :Use
quote: "new_panel() is used to created panels"; "Mainpulate the panels"; "removes it form the stack"; "Entered Resizing :Use Arrow Keys...".
earlier: Each fragment is simply misspelled/misphrased English; no further source changes that.

claim: `bottom_panel` on a hidden panel()
quote: Intro wraps the ban as "top_panel() or bottom_panel on a hidden panel()". bottom_panel() will insert an unlinked (hidden) panel at the bottom of the stack.
earlier: Taking the intro fragment at face value would match; p_bottom.c shows hidden panels can be bottom_panel'd.

claim: In the `cbreak()` mode these control characters are interpreted as any other character by the terminal driver
quote: HOWTO attributes pass-through of CTRL-Z/CTRL-C to cbreak(). curs_inopts(3X): in cbreak mode interrupt/quit/suspend/flow characters "are unaffected"; raw mode "passes through" those characters uninterpreted.
earlier: HOWTO alone would match the claim as printed; the man page shows HOWTO swapped cbreak and raw.

claim: `endwin()` frees the memory taken by curses sub-system and its data structures and puts the terminal in normal mode
quote: HOWTO says endwin frees curses memory and restores the terminal. curs_initscr(3X): endwin restores the terminal, and "Calling endwin does not dispose of the memory allocated by initscr or newterm."
earlier: Terminal restoration matches; the free-memory half is contradicted only once the man page HISTORY/NOTES are opened.

claim: `<curses.h>` also includes `<termios.h>`, `<termio.h>`, or `<sgtty.h>` depending on your system
quote: Intro claims curses.h includes termios/termio/sgtty. curses.h.in includes <stdio.h> and does not include those tty headers.
earlier: The intro statement would stand until curses.h.in is opened.

claim: In linking with `curses` you need to have `-lncurses` ... There is no need for any other libraries
quote: Intro: "In linking with curses you need to have -lncurses ... There is no need for any other libraries." That holds for the basic libcurses/ncurses case the paragraph describes; higher-level HOWTO examples separately add -lmenu/-lpanel.
earlier: Without noting the intro's basic-curses scope I might disagree because menu/panel need extra libs; those are outside this sentence's context.

claim: To use ncurses library functions, you have to include ncurses.h in your programs
quote: HOWTO: "include ncurses.h". Intro and the shipped header are curses.h; INSTALL documents an optional install-as-ncurses.h mode, not the default requirement.
earlier: HOWTO alone would match; curses.h.in/headers and the intro's #include <curses.h> contradict 'have to include ncurses.h'.

claim: `bool`: boolean type, actually a "char"
quote: Intro: "boolean type, actually a char". curses.h.in uses NCURSES_BOOL from configure (stdbool.h, C++ bool, or a configured type), not an unconditional char.
earlier: The intro claim looks definitive until the configurable bool typedef is opened.

claim: `OK`: error flag returned by routines when things go right
quote: Intro defines OK as the "error flag returned by routines when things go right." curses.h.in has #define OK (0), the success return paired with ERR.
earlier: Calling a success code an 'error flag' sounds wrong in isolation; the header confirms OK is the success return the intro describes.
